name: Tecture IO
description:
Tecture is an architecture documentation format — flat JSON + Markdown authored and maintained by coding agents — plus viewers that render those files as interactive, drill-down diagrams. A coding agent writes a manifest, one diagram file per C4 level, and one Markdown description per node into an architecture/ directory that lives in the repo beside the code; either viewer reads that tree on demand and renders it.

The repo is a pnpm monorepo of six packages. @tecture/shared is the contract core: the file-format and API types, the ArchitectureDataSource and LayoutStore interfaces every backend implements, the REST/postMessage request and response shapes, and the source-independent validators and helpers (normalizeLayoutUpdate, buildArchitectureSummary, findNode, buildSourceUrl). @tecture/web is the React + Vite + ReactFlow UI. Two viewer hosts embed that same UI: @tecture/core (the npm-published CLI that boots an Express server) and tecture-vscode (the VS Code Marketplace extension). Two installer packages distribute the authoring side: @tecture/skill is a pure, zero-dependency CLI that copies the architecture-docs skill into a developer's coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Windsurf), and @tecture/install — the primary entry point — reuses it as a library and additionally sets up the mandatory CodeGraph companion (installs the @colbymchenry/codegraph CLI globally, configures its MCP server for supported agents, and indexes the repo). The skill hard-requires that companion: discovery and deep-dives query the CodeGraph index, and a bundled evidence script verifies every node path and declared edge against it, writing a committed drift report (architecture/.tecture/drift.json) that both viewers render as a Drift panel with per-node Evidence sections.

Both hosts read the same architecture/ directory and implement the same data-source contract, so they render identical diagrams; they differ only in transport and file access. The CLI serves the bundled SPA and a REST API over HTTP on port 3000 and reads the filesystem with node:fs. The extension hosts the SPA in a webview, answers postMessage requests in the extension host, and reads files through vscode.workspace.fs — adding a sidebar diagram tree, file watchers that live-reload on disk changes, and the ability to open a node's source file in the editor.

There are no datastores and no authentication. External dependencies are PostHog Cloud, which receives anonymous, opt-out usage telemetry from the CLI viewer, the VS Code extension, and both installers — disabled by DO_NOT_TRACK or TECTURE_TELEMETRY, and never carrying architecture content — and CodeGraph, the local code-intelligence index Tecture installs and reads entirely on the developer's machine (its own telemetry is disabled per spawn). The only durable state is the flat tree of JSON + Markdown in the developer's own repository, plus optional node-layout positions persisted under architecture/.tecture. Coding agents write the tree with ordinary file writes; either viewer reads it on demand.
